::: {.standfirst}
I get language models into products at Microsoft — designing the systems around
them, fine-tuning them for the job, and wiring them into Word, PowerPoint, Excel,
OneNote, and Teams. The other half of the work is knowing whether any of it is actually
good, which is why I also lead evaluation for the Office Copilots: benchmarks,
judge models, and the failure taxonomies that come out the other side.
:::

Eleven plus years of shipping software/models — four as a data scientist at Penske Logistics
owning freight-pricing and driver-safety systems end to end, and three before
that writing C/C++ for automotive infotainment. Mostly I've worked on the
unglamorous middle: the architecture, orchestration, and plumbing between a model
that works in a notebook and one that works for millions of people.

::: {.eyebrow}
writing
:::

I'm extending Jay Mody's picoGPT — GPT-2 in NumPy, no PyTorch or TensorFlow — with the parts a real inference system needs: batching, variable-length batching, a KV cache, sampling, and the scheduling and memory tricks that come after. Each post ends by proving the new version still matches the old one.
